name: Trade war & tariffs
summary: Trump's 12 Nov threat to double tariffs on Mexico stands; no deadline or increase in force by 17 Nov
state: On 12 Nov President Trump said he would double US tariffs on Mexico unless it stops migrant caravans, without naming a deadline, a mechanism or the products covered; Mexican vehicles face 25% duties and steel and aluminium 50% (KATV, 12 Nov). Searches to 17 Nov found no tariff increase in force and no retaliation. Leaders meet at APEC in Shenzhen from 17 Nov. Watch holds: a major rise is threatened but not imposed.
for_you: Firms trading with Mexico, especially in vehicles, steel and aluminium, are most exposed if the threat is carried out. Prices of affected goods tend to follow tariff changes with a lag.
rubric_hit: New major tariff threatened between large economies (US on Mexico, 12 Nov) = Watch; nothing new in force

sources.title: Trump threatens to double tariffs on Mexico if it fails to stop migrant caravan

why: Tariffs raise prices, reroute supply chains and slow growth; escalation cycles hurt export-heavy economies like the UK's partners.
drivers: US tariff policy, retaliation, court rulings, trade deals, WTO disputes.

rubric.alert: Broad new tariffs in force with retaliation under way, or US average effective tariff rising sharply.
rubric.watch: New major tariffs announced or threatened between large economies.
rubric.normal: Tariff regime stable; no new major measures in the past two weeks.
